question: In Primary Health Care, what does public participation actually mean?

options.A: Communities actively shaping and sharing responsibility for their health services
options.B: Government agencies taking full control of all village health clinics
options.C: Midwives making all health decisions without consulting village elders
options.D: Patients paying higher user fees to access maternity care services

explanation: Public participation means community members are active partners rather than passive recipients of healthcare services. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is community involvement a core principle of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It allows midwives to transfer all administrative duties to local youths
options.B: It forces traditional birth attendants to stop practicing immediately
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for government funding in rural clinics
options.D: It ensures health programs fit local cultural realities and actual needs

explanation: When local people are involved, health interventions are better tailored to suit their customs, beliefs, and daily living conditions. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h1)

question: At what stages of a health project should community involvement happen?

options.A: Strictly during the final evaluation report writing
options.B: Only after the government finishes building the clinic
options.C: Only when emergency funds run out unexpectedly
options.D: During both planning and implementation phases

explanation: True participation means community members are involved right from the initial planning stages through to executing the health activities. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of having a community contribute labor or resources to a local health project?

options.A: It guarantees that no maternal complications will ever occur in that village
options.B: It fosters a strong sense of ownership and protects the project's future
options.C: It reduces the professional training requirements needed for practicing midwives
options.D: It completely removes the responsibility of supervision from the local government

explanation: When communities invest their own resources and effort, they value the facility more and work harder to sustain it. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h2)

question: What does local ownership mean for a community health facility?

options.A: The community views the facility as their own and takes responsibility for it
options.B: Foreign donor agencies hand over financial audits to village chiefs
options.C: The local government transfers the land title directly to the attending midwife
options.D: Private businessmen take over the daily management of pharmacy supplies

explanation: Local ownership means the community takes pride in and responsibility for the health facility and its services. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h3)

question: A rural clinic notices low antenatal attendance during planting season because women are busy on farms. What action best shows community-driven problem solving?

options.A: Reporting all pregnant women who miss appointments to local police authorities
options.B: Closing the clinic temporarily until the farming season comes to a complete end
options.C: Meeting with women and village leaders to reschedule clinics to market days or evenings
options.D: Handing out heavy financial fines to families who fail to attend morning clinic

explanation: Collaborating with the community to adapt clinic schedules to their livelihood demonstrates practical problem-solving based on local needs. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to community engagement in health programs?

options.A: Excessive availability of trained midwives in rural villages
options.B: Domination of local meetings by wealthy or powerful elites
options.C: Poverty forcing families to prioritize daily economic survival
options.D: High levels of illiteracy and language barriers

explanation: A surplus of midwives is generally not a barrier; rather, staff shortages are a frequent challenge in rural Nigerian health settings. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does poor financial accountability in a local health committee affect public participation?

options.A: It encourages the government to increase monthly budgetary allocations
options.B: It has no measurable impact on how villagers view primary health care
options.C: It forces community members to volunteer more time for construction work
options.D: It destroys community trust and discourages further public contributions

explanation: When people suspect financial mismanagement of user fees or donations, they lose faith and refuse to support subsequent health initiatives. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which traditional method remains very effective for spreading health messages in remote rural villages?
explanation: Town criers are a trusted, traditional communication channel that easily reaches every corner of a remote rural settlement. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h5)

question: A midwife wants to mobilize busy market women for a maternal health campaign. What is the most effective approach?

options.A: Issuing strict warning letters to traders who miss scheduled morning lectures
options.B: Waiting inside the clinic office for market women to walk in and ask for pamphlets
options.C: Publishing long technical notices on government websites that require internet access
options.D: Visiting market association leaders to arrange brief health talks during their regular meetings

explanation: Going directly to where market women gather and working through their existing leadership ensures maximum participation without disrupting their livelihoods. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h5)

question: What primary role does a midwife play in community-level health action?

options.A: Enforcing strict health laws without consulting community elders
options.B: Financing all community development projects out of personal salary
options.C: Acting as a bridge and facilitator between the community and the health system
options.D: Taking over local political leadership positions in the village council

explanation: The midwife connects professional healthcare services with local community members, facilitating mutual understanding and cooperation. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why should a midwife collaborate with traditional birth attendants instead of showing hostility?

options.A: Ministry regulations require midwives to hand over their clinic licenses to them
options.B: It prevents traditional attendants from practicing herbal medicine in private homes
options.C: Collaboration builds mutual trust and encourages safe, timely referrals of complications
options.D: Traditional birth attendants possess superior clinical training in surgical procedures

explanation: Working alongside traditional birth attendants helps bridge the gap, ensuring they bring complicated cases to the clinic early rather than hiding them. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h6)
